children: The latest Bank of England money and credit data shows above-forecast rise in U.K. consumer credit in July, indicating households' resilience, Capital Economics' Ruth Gregory says in a note. Consumer credit rose by 2 billion pounds ($2.71 billion) in July, above the 1.8 billion pounds consensus forecast by economists in a WSJ poll. "This suggests households are willing to offset some of the hit to their real incomes by borrowing more." The data come as yields on 30-year U.K. government bonds rise to their highest since 1998. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
